references.text: Here the same three types of skin diseases are introduced: swelling (שְׂאֵת), eruption (סַפַּחַת), and bright spots (בֶּהֶרֶת). This is the first occurrence of these terms, which Leviticus 14:56 summarizes.
Mentions swelling (שְׂאֵת) and bright spots (בֶּהֶרֶת) in connection with diagnosing skin diseases.
Describes the swelling (שְׂאֵת) on the head as white-reddish, similar to leprosy on the skin.
The immediate context that introduces the summary of the laws concerning leprosy, including references to various types of skin diseases and mold in houses.
Reminder to follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy, referring back to the laws in Leviticus 13–14.
